name: T19 cohort and persona live proof
description: A minimal real execution that gates one context on two specialist validator assignments with distinct profiles and staffs the implementer with a non-default profile.

charter.mission: Deliver a tiny greeting module in this scratch repository so that a real graph execution exercises a two-specialist validator cohort and a non-default implementer profile end to end.

invariants.statement: Use plain CommonJS and Node's built-in test runner only; add no dependencies, no package manager files, and no build step.

sourcesOfTruth.label: The execution context acceptance criteria
sourcesOfTruth.description: The literal acceptance criteria of the greeting context are the governing contract for both the implementer and every validator.

sourcesOfTruth.label: Scratch repository README
sourcesOfTruth.description: Describes what this scratch repository is for.

executionContexts.title: Greeting module
executionContexts.description: Add a greeting function and its Node test-runner tests to the repository root.
executionContexts.acceptanceCriteria:
1. A file `greet.js` exists at the repository root, is valid CommonJS, and sets `module.exports = { greet }` where `greet` takes one argument `name`.
2. `greet("World")` returns exactly the string `Hello, World!`.
3. `greet("")` returns exactly the string `Hello, stranger!`.
4. A file `greet.test.js` exists at the repository root, uses Node's built-in `node:test` and `node:assert/strict`, and contains one assertion for the named case in criterion 2 and one assertion for the empty-name case in criterion 3.
5. `node --test` passes in the repository root with no failing tests.

assignments.focus: the exported shape in criterion 1 and the exact returned strings in criteria 2 and 3
the test file required by criterion 4 and the passing run required by criterion 5

tasks.title: Add the greet module
tasks.instructions: Create `greet.js` at the repository root. It must be plain CommonJS: define `function greet(name)` and end the file with `module.exports = { greet };`. When `name` is a non-empty string, return `Hello, ${name}!`. When `name` is an empty string, return `Hello, stranger!`. Add no dependencies and no package.json.

tasks.title: Add the greet tests
tasks.instructions: Create `greet.test.js` at the repository root using Node's built-in runner: `const test = require('node:test');` and `const assert = require('node:assert/strict');`. Write one test asserting `greet('World') === 'Hello, World!'` and one test asserting `greet('') === 'Hello, stranger!'`. Run `node --test` in the repository root and confirm both tests pass before completing this task.
